aggressive_definition: Advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive incident prostate cancer outcomes.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Conditional logistic regression was used to examine the association between melatonin levels and the development of prostate cancer outcomes (all incident cases, advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive), overall and by race/ethnicity.
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Multiethnic Cohort using prediagnostic urine samples.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes all incident prostate cancer and several aggressive incident outcomes, including advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive disease. It reports 1,263 total cases and counts for some overlapping aggressive subtypes, but no single count for the broad aggressive endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Conditional logistic regression was used to examine the association between melatonin levels and the development of prostate cancer outcomes (all incident cases, advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive), overall and by race/ethnicity.
estimate_classifications.reason: The existing estimate is explicitly identified as overall incident prostate cancer. It must not be relabeled aggressive merely because the study also analyzed aggressive outcomes.

additional_estimates.comparison: Urinary melatonin levels in relation to advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive prostate cancer outcomes; specific contrast not reported in the abstract.
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Among 1,263 cases, 135 were advanced stage, 101 were lethal cases, and 282 were high-grade disease. Median melatonin levels were similar in controls [17.12 ng/mL; interquartile range (IQR), 19.78] and cases (17.93 ng/mL; IQR, 19.76), and we found no significant association between urinary melatonin levels and prostate cancer risk overall or in any clinical or racial subgroup.
